# bugs #3527: sdas evaluates constants as 24-bit signed values, so a shift by 24 gives 0x00 or 0xFF

- Ticket: https://sourceforge.net/p/sdcc/bugs/3527/
- Category: [Duplicates](../../duplicate.md)
- Evidence: tested on r17176
- Recommended action: Close as a duplicate of bug #4070. Add the two constants of this ticket to the test for that fix.
<!-- end of generated block -->

## Finding

The defect reproduces on r17176 with sdas8051 and sdasstm8. `.db (0x12345678)>>24` assembles to
0x00, and `.db (16000000)>>24` assembles to 0xFF. These are the two results in the ticket, and the
correct bytes are 0x12 and 0x00. 0x007FFFFF shifted by 24 gives 0x00 and 0x00800000 gives 0xFF, so
bit 23 is the sign bit. sdasz80 assembles the correct bytes for the four lines.

The listing in the ticket is from a pdk assembler. The pdk assemblers were not built for this test.

## Reason

Bug #4070 reports a wrong address byte for an mcs51 `__sfr32`, which sdcc writes as
`(_X >> 24) & 0xFF`. The two tickets have one cause. `term` in `sdas/asxxsrc/asexpr.c` stores
every constant through `rngchk`, which sign-extends the value from the width that `exprmasks` set.
The `>>` operator then shifts the 32-bit value. as8051, asstm8, and the pdk assemblers call
`exprmasks(3)`, and asz80 calls `exprmasks(4)`. In the sdas8051 test, `(X >> 24) & 0xFF` with
`X = 0xa3a5a6a7` also assembled to 0xFF, which is the case of bug #4070.

A maintainer names the common cause in the first comment. Bug #4070 is open and has the analysis,
a patch, and the discussion of the design.
